questions.question: Explain the difference between a return and an allowance, and state exactly when the Cost of Sales column of the DAJ is used.
questions.expected_answer: A return means goods physically come back to the business; an allowance means the customer keeps the goods and only the price is reduced. The Cost of Sales column writes only for returns of saleable goods — the cost goes back into Trading Stock and out of Cost of Sales. For an allowance no goods move, so the cost column stays empty. Follow the goods, not the money.

questions.question: Show how the list of debtors is tested against Debtors Control for Lindi's month, naming the figures.
questions.expected_answer: Personal balances: M. Sithole R2 700 (2 400 plus 900 less 600) and P. Govender R1 600 (1 800 less 200), so the list totals R4 300. Debtors Control shows debits of R5 100 from the DJ and credits of R800 from the DAJ, a balance of R4 300 debit. The two must agree because the control account carries the totals of the same journals whose lines built the personal accounts.

questions.question: Why are credit sales still credited to the Sales account, and why do personal accounts get posted daily while control gets totals monthly?
questions.expected_answer: A sale is income when it is earned, regardless of when the money arrives, so credit sales credit Sales immediately. Personal accounts are posted daily because a debtor's balance must be current whenever they ask; the control account and other general ledger accounts receive monthly totals because the ledger needs summaries, not every line — detail daily, summary monthly.
